Countdown to Friday begins! Today's newsletter, edited by Herb Scribner, is 977 words, a 3½-min. read. Thanks to Sheryl Miller for copy editing.

⛰️ Exclusive: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent made the case for lighter financial regulation at the G20 finance ministers gathering in the Blue Ridge Mountains today, telling CEOs that post-crisis rules have squeezed small banks.

  • Bessent said in Asheville, N.C.: "To expand opportunity for all Americans, the banks that serve Main Street must have the same chance to succeed as those that serve Wall Street." More from Courtenay Brown.

⚡ Situational awareness: President Trump and his senior aides have been considering waging limited strikes in the Strait of Hormuz to curb future attacks from Iran, Axios' Barak Ravid reports.
 
 
1 big thing: Trump: "Let data reign"
 
Illustration: Brendan Lynch/Axios. Stock: Getty Images

🤖 President Trump has a new message for Americans rebelling over the nation's data center boom: Get over it.

  • Trump warned Monday: "If we kill the Golden Goose, you will only have yourselves to blame."

🗳️ Why it matters: Nine weeks out from the midterms, the president is charging into a fight Republicans have been scrambling to escape — staking political capital on one of the most toxic issues in the country, Axios' Zachary Basu writes.

Trump wrote on Truth Social: "The only reason that communities throughout the U.S.A. should not want Data Centers is if they want to end up being backwards and poor."

  • "If they want to be successful and rich, with far lower taxes and jobs all over the place, let Data Reign," he added.

🤝 Trump's blunt intervention comes as the AI industry mounts a far more disciplined campaign to persuade data center skeptics rather than browbeat them.

  • Build American AI, an advocacy group linked to the pro-AI super PAC Leading the Future, is ready to unload a $50 million war chest to defend data centers in key states, starting in Kansas, Ohio and Wisconsin.

🔎 Zoom in: Prominent investor Gavin Baker laid out his own six-part case for data centers on X, which was quickly amplified by Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and other tech leaders.

  • 💧 Water: Newer facilities can sharply reduce freshwater use through closed-loop cooling and recycled water, Baker argues. He says those systems should be required for new projects.
  • 💸 Taxes: Data centers can generate enormous property-tax revenue for local governments, Baker says, potentially outweighing the sales-tax exemptions that have drawn criticism.
  • 💪 Jobs: The buildout is driving demand for electricians, plumbers, welders, HVAC technicians and contractors, making building-trade unions some of the industry's most important allies.
  • 🔌 Power: Baker points to new large-load tariffs and ratepayer-protection agreements as a way to ensure data centers, rather than existing customers, pay for the new generation and grid capacity they require.
  • ☀️ Environment: Baker argues that natural gas, renewables and batteries can meet surging demand now, with data centers ultimately moving toward solar and storage.
  • 🌆 Towns: Data centers can turn struggling communities into beneficiaries of the AI boom. Baker points to Quincy, Washington, where data centers now account for more than half of the local property-tax base.

🥊 Reality check: Republicans in key battlegrounds have spent weeks recalibrating their positions on data centers as the issue turned politically toxic. Trump's intervention risks blowing up that escape route.

2. ⛽ 100 gallons of gas on a chart
 
Data: U.S. Energy Information Administration. (Each week compares the cost of 100 gallons at that week's price with the cost of 100 gallons at the price at the beginning of the conflict.) Chart: Andrew Pantazi/Axios

Higher gasoline prices in the first six months of the Iran conflict have cost U.S. drivers far more than they did over the same period after Russia's invasion of Ukraine, Axios' Ben Geman and Andrew Pantazi report.

  • Yes, gasoline hit an all-time high of over $5 per gallon under the Biden administration. But the elevation since the Iran war began has been more persistent.

🎨 The big picture: Axios tracked what 100 gallons of gas cost each week during the first six months of the Iran and Ukraine conflicts, compared with prices just before each war began.

  • The cumulative extra cost of gasoline is substantially higher now.

👀 What we're watching: The average U.S. gasoline price hit $4.08 today, according to AAA.

  • Prices will likely be near or above $4 per gallon on Labor Day weekend.

3. ⚡️ Catch me up
 
A man adds photos of his missing relative to a wall outside Tribhuvan University Teaching Hospital, in Kathmandu, Nepal, today. Photo: Monika Mall/Reuters
  1. 🌊 Hundreds of workers are believed to be trapped in tunnels at hydropower sites buried in mud by catastrophic flooding on the Nepal-China border. Deaths have passed 950, and 4,400+ people are missing. Get the latest.
  2. ⚽ Josh Kushner is speaking publicly for the first time about his failed FIFA deal, saying in a statement to Axios that his venture capital firm Thrive "failed to appreciate the political dynamics of global football. ... Had we known what this would devolve into, we would not have gotten involved." More from Dan Primack.
  3. ❌ Kalshi issued its first-ever lifetime ban today to former Rep. George Santos of New York, after he allegedly made bets on his own appearance at President Trump's State of the Union address. Go deeper.
  4. 🍎 President Trump personally asked Apple to rename Lake Ontario "Lake America" on Apple Maps, days after Google changed the lake's name on its maps app. Get the latest.
 
 
4. 🇦🇷 1 for the road: Messi waves goodbye
 
Lionel Messi in an Argentina jersey, walking off the field after the World Cup Final in July. Photo: Hannah Peters/FIFA via Getty Images

Lionel Messi announced today that he's retiring from Argentina's national soccer team.

  • 🐐 Messi is widely regarded as one of the greatest soccer players ever, along with Pelé and Maradona.

📱 Messi wrote on his Instagram account: "It was a decision that hurt, and still hurts deeply, but I understand that the time has come."

  • "I swear to you that I always gave it my all, not just in these last few years when we won everything, but before that too. I always fought and left everything on the field for this jersey, to bring you joy and make you feel proud to be Argentine through football."

🌟 Stunning stat: Messi will end his international career tied with longtime rival Cristiano Ronaldo for the most World Cup tournament appearances (six) in history, The Athletic reports (gift link).
